annotation.title_clean: Buffer or Bottleneck? Employment Exposure to Generative AI and the Digital Divide in Latin America
annotation.title_en: Buffer or Bottleneck? Employment Exposure to Generative AI and the Digital Divide in Latin America
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Gmyrek, P.; Winkler, H.; Garganta, S.
annotation.venue: ILO Working Paper 121 (ILO and World Bank)
annotation.summary_en: ILO/World Bank working paper estimating Latin American employment exposure to generative AI (automation and augmentation) using household and labour surveys, adjusted for computer access at work. Finds the digital divide blocks nearly half of augmentable jobs, especially in poorer countries. Not about robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Exposure to GenAI is higher for urban, formal, higher-educated, higher-income jobs.
Younger workers face greater exposure, including automation risk in finance, insurance and public administration.
Nearly half of jobs with augmentation potential lack digital technology use at work.
Digital divide effect is stronger in poorer countries.
Exposure estimates are adjusted for computer access to reflect slower technology adoption.
